one_liner: Broad BSD-licensed C++20 crypto toolkit; maintainer reports faster small-message AES-128-GCM than OpenSSL 3.6.0 on one Skylake.
what_it_does: Botan is a general-purpose C++20 cryptography library covering TLS 1.2/1.3, X.509, classical and post-quantum public-key schemes, and many AEAD modes (GCM, GCM-SIV from 3.13.0, OCB, EAX, SIV, CCM, ChaCha20Poly1305), with C (FFI) and Python APIs. AEAD use goes through AEAD_Mode::create("AES-128/GCM", Cipher_Dir::Encryption), then set_key(), optional set_associated_data(), and per message start(nonce) and finish(buffer), which appends the tag to a secure_vector in place. It is not a drop-in for OpenSSL EVP: algorithms are named by strings, objects are stateful C++ classes, and the build is configured per module with configure.py.
how_it_is_fast: AES and GHASH are separate kernels picked at run time by CPUID: AES uses VAES with AVX2 (8 blocks in flight), AES-NI or ARMv8 AES (4 blocks), POWER8, vperm SIMD, or a bitsliced constant-time fallback; GHASH uses CLMUL/PMULL with 4 or 8 precomputed powers of H, or AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ with 16 precomputed powers (aggregated reduction; new GCM/GMAC AVX-512 paths landed in 3.11.0). GCM runs two passes over the buffer, CTR keystream then GHASH, rather than OpenSSL's stitched AES+GHASH loop, which the maintainer names as the remaining large-message gap. The small-message advantage claimed in issue #969 comes from per-message setup cost, not from the kernels (see gotchas).
when_to_use: C++20 code bases that want one permissively licensed library for AEAD, TLS 1.3, X.509 and post-quantum schemes (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FrodoKEM) behind a single modern C++ API, with C and Python bindings.
Bulk AES-GCM on AVX-512 CPUs with Botan 3.11 or later: on a Ryzen 9 7950X3D the original poster measured 0.38 cycles/byte at 16 KiB, within about 1.5x of OpenSSL 4.0.1, down from 12x in 2017.
Many messages under one long-lived key where AEAD is not the bottleneck (TLS records, file encryption), since key setup and associated data can be done once and only start()/finish() run per message.
Targets without AES instructions that still need constant-time AES: the bitsliced and vperm fallbacks avoid table lookups.
Builds that need a trimmed footprint: configure.py --minimized-build --enable-modules=... or the single-file amalgamation.
when_not_to_use: Maximum bulk AES-GCM throughput: OpenSSL is about 1.65x faster at 16 KiB on the maintainer's Skylake and about 1.5x on Zen 4 in the same thread, because Botan's GCM is not stitched.

Tiny messages with a new nonce each: every start() precomputes a full keystream batch (256 bytes with AES-NI, 512 bytes with VAES), so a 16-byte message costs 16 or 32 AES blocks; the Zen 4 run measured 54.84 cycles/byte at 16 B against OpenSSL's 20.31.
Projects that need OpenSSL's EVP/C ABI, provider model or engines; Botan's C FFI is its own API.
Toolchains older than C++20: Botan 3 needs GCC 11.2+, Clang 14+, Visual C++ 2022, Xcode 15+ or NDK 26; Botan 2 reached end of life on 2025-01-01.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib built with configure.py, or a single-file amalgamation; also packaged by most distributions
integration.dependencies: none required; optional zlib, bzip2, lzma (compression API), SQLite (certificate store), PKCS#11, TPM 2.0 and ESDM modules
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; tier-1 GCC 11.2+, Clang 14+, Visual C++ 2022; Xcode 15+ and NDK 26 on Apple and Android
integration.platforms: tier-1 Linux x86-64, aarch64 and ppc64le, Windows x86-64; tier-2 macOS, iOS, Android, Linux arm32 and x86-32, FreeBSD, MinGW; WebAssembly SIMD paths since 3.11.0; runtime CPUID dispatch for AES-NI, VAES, AVX-512 CLMUL, ARMv8 and POWER8
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in the files read; cipher mode objects hold per-message state (nonce, AD, GHASH accumulator), so use one object per thread.

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the claim: `botan speed` (src/cli/perf_sym.cpp) calls set_key() once outside the timer and times only start(iv) plus finish() per message, while OpenSSL 3.6.0 `openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm` runs EVP_Update_loop_aead_enc for every GCM cipher, calling EVP_CipherInit_ex(ctx, NULL, NULL, key, aead_iv, -1) per message, which re-runs AES key expansion and CRYPTO_gcm128_init. The 16-256 B rows therefore charge OpenSSL a re-key per message that Botan never pays. OpenSSL 1.1.0e's speed tool instead streamed EVP_EncryptUpdate with no per-message init or tag, so the 'OpenSSL regressed since 1.1.0' small-message comparison in the thread partly reflects a change in what the tool measures.

Per-message fixed cost: GCM start() calls CTR_BE::set_iv, whose seek(0) encrypts parallel_bytes() of keystream (parallelism x 16 B x ParallelismMult 4: 256 B on AES-NI, 512 B on VAES) even for a 16-byte message.

Associated data must be set after set_key() and before start() and persists across messages; calling it after start() throws (GHASH::set_associated_data checks BOTAN_STATE_CHECK(!m_nonce)). The scc-tw/cryptobench-cpp adapter makes exactly this mistake, which is why every Botan 3.9.0 AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 row in its result.json reads 'Encryption failed'; its CBC rows fail because the --minimized-build module list omits cbc. That suite therefore has no valid Botan AEAD data.

The 3.11.0 release introduced a certificate verification bypass (CVE-2026-34580) fixed in 3.11.1, the version the maintainer benchmarked; 3.12.0 added maximum input length limits for ChaCha20Poly1305 and GHASH/GCM. Stay on the latest 3.x release.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Botan over Mbed TLS when you run on desktop or server CPUs and want pipelined AES-NI/VAES and aggregated GHASH (Mbed TLS GCM does one block at a time), or over Crypto++ when you want a C++20 API with quarterly releases and post-quantum and TLS 1.3 support in the same library. For raw AEAD speed, a dedicated library such as chacha20poly1305-simd, hardware-rust-crypto or libaegis (if you can change cipher) is faster.
verified_claims_summary: The maintainer's Mar 31 2026 comment on issue #969 compares Botan 3.11.1 `botan speed` with OpenSSL 3.6.0 `openssl speed -seconds 1 -evp aes-128-gcm` on an i7-6700K at 4 GHz (compiler and flags not stated): Botan is about 1.5x faster at 16 B and 64 B and 1.2x at 256 B, OpenSSL about 1.65x faster at 16 KiB (derived from page data), with the two tools timing different per-message work. The only fully specified run in the thread (Jul 22 2026, Botan 3.12.0 with gcc 15.3 against OpenSSL 4.0.1 with gcc 16, -march=znver4, Ryzen 9 7950X3D at 4.2 GHz) has Botan slower at every size, 54.84 vs 20.31 cycles/byte at 16 B and 0.38 vs 0.25 at 16 KiB.
status_note: Actively developed (3.13.0 released 2026-08-13, quarterly minor releases, last commit 2026-10-10, 3.3k stars), BSD-2-Clause and copyable; the small-message speed claim rests on one maintainer machine and an unequal tool comparison.
